Subject: Inquiry: education/nonprofit credits for student research lab

Hi Ben,

I manage grants for the Student AI Lab at LabForward University. We're launching a semester-long research cohort (15 student projects) that will be using hosted API access for data augmentation and model-assisted literature reviews. Budget is tight — several projects are funded by small department grants and external donations.

Two quick questions: 1) Do you have an academic/nonprofit pricing tier for the Redwood hosted API? 2) Is there a process for a one-off pricing exception or credits for student-run labs?

Estimated consumption: ~20M tokens/month initially, potentially scaling to 60M/month over the semester. We can provide 501(c)(3) documentation and a short project outline.

Thanks — I appreciate any guidance.

Best,
Anna Ruiz
Grants Coordinator, Student AI Lab
LabForward University

Subject: Re: Inquiry: education/nonprofit credits for student research lab

Hi Anna — thanks for reaching out and congrats on the cohort. Short answers up front: yes, we do have an academic pricing path, and yes — we can consider one-time credit packages for student labs on a case-by-case basis.

A few clarifying items so I can move this to approvals:
- Can you confirm nonprofit status (tax-exempt/501c) and provide a short one-page project summary (goals + timeline)?
- Expected peak concurrency / latency sensitivity (are you doing interactive chat demos or bulk batch generation?).
- Preferred procurement flow (do you need a PO or will a credit memo suffice?).

What tends to work for labs like yours: we can offer a "Starter Academic Grant" — a bundle of credits that functions as a hosted API dollar credit applied to the account. Typical structure: 60% credit (i.e., customer pays 40% of list) applied to the first 9 months or up to $25k consumed, whichever comes first. For a stronger case (university program with multiple faculty sponsors and 501(c) evidence) we can escalate to a one-time 65% credit for 12 months — requires manager approval and a short SOW.

I've attached a short eligibility checklist to speed things up. If you can send the 501(c) and project outline I'll open the exception request.

Next step: if you can share the docs, I will prepare a formal quote and loop in our grants reviewer.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Account Executive — Education & Nonprofit
Redwood Inference
